result.notes:
I wrote 5 API tests and 2 browser tests. On this commit all 5 API tests fail with AssertionError and nothing else. The browser tests collect but have not been run.

Results:
- `.venv/bin/python -m pytest -p no:cacheprovider bookmarks/tests/test_bundle_filters_blind_2_api.py` → `5 failed in 0.95s`. Two say `'filter_unread' not found in {...}` and three say `Lists differ: [1, 2, 3, 4, 5] != [1, 2, 3]` (or `[1, 2, 3, 4] != [1]`). There were no import, name, attribute, key or type errors and no server errors.
- `--collect-only -q -o "python_files=e2e_test_*.py" bookmarks/tests_e2e/e2e_test_bundle_filters_blind_2.py` → `2 tests collected`. I have not verified that the browser tests pass, because the assets aren't built here.
- `ruff format` reformatted the browser test file (formatting only), and `ruff check` reported "All checks passed!" on both files.
- I added a temporary test file to confirm the bookmark-page checks work when they run (logging the API client in with a session, the list-assertion mixin). It passed and I deleted it, so only the two files above remain.

**API file: `bookmarks/tests/test_bundle_filters_blind_2_api.py`** (`LinkdingApiTestCase`, `BookmarkFactoryMixin`, `BookmarkListTestMixin`)
The strategy puts most coverage at the API level because it is fast and sees the behaviour directly. `setup_bundle` doesn't accept the new fields at this commit, so every filtered bundle is created with `POST /api/bundles/`. Before the change that request still returns 201 and the new fields are dropped, so the tests fail on an assertion, not on the status code. Fields are checked with `assertIn` before they are read, and result sets are compared as sorted id lists so creation order doesn't matter.
- `test_create_and_get_bundle_with_filter_unread_and_filter_shared` (AC1): the posted values (yes/no and no/yes) are returned by `GET /api/bundles/<id>/` and by the list endpoint. A bundle posted without them returns "off" for both.
- `test_patch_bundle_changes_filter_fields_and_keeps_others` (AC2): patching one field leaves the other unchanged, patching both changes both, and resetting to off works. Name, search and the three tag fields don't change.
- `test_bookmarks_by_bundle_filter_unread_yes_no_off` (AC3): read and unread bookmarks that match the bundle's search, plus decoys that don't. Checks the exact result of `GET /api/bookmarks/?bundle=<id>` for yes, no and off. The "off" case also proves the search condition still applies.
- `test_bookmarks_by_bundle_filter_shared_yes_no_off` (AC4): the same for shared and unshared bookmarks.
- `test_bookmarks_by_bundle_combines_unread_shared_search_and_tags` (AC5): all four read/shared combinations, plus decoys that fail only the search, only the required tag or only the excluded tag. Three bundles are checked: yes/yes, no/no and yes/off. The yes/yes and no/no bundles are also opened on `/bookmarks?bundle=<id>` with a logged-in session, so the page's bookmark list is checked here instead of in a browser test.

**Browser file: `bookmarks/tests_e2e/e2e_test_bundle_filters_blind_2.py`** (`LinkdingE2ETestCase`)
The strategy allows one or two browser tests for the path a user sees, and the form is the only part of this ticket a user sees. There are two tests because creating and editing are separate paths. The edit path can't start from an already filtered bundle without new helper arguments. Sharing is switched on in the test user's profile in case the implementation only shows the sharing dropdown then. Fixture bookmarks are 2 unread+shared, 1 unread+unshared, 1 read+shared and 3 read+unshared, so the "Found N" count changes at every step (7 → 3 → 2 when creating, 7 → 3 when editing) and never needs the singular form. Options are chosen by their visible label, and saved choices are checked through the selected option's text, because the ticket doesn't fix the form's option values.
- `test_create_bundle_with_reading_and_sharing_state`: on `/bundles/new` it first checks that both dropdowns exist with the options All/Unread/Read and All/Shared/Unshared, and that both default to All. It then picks Unread and checks the preview count and list, picks Shared and checks them again, saves, and confirms that `/bookmarks?bundle=<id>` lists only the unread shared bookmarks. Finally it reopens the edit form and checks that Unread and Shared are selected and the preview shows 2.
- `test_edit_bundle_reading_and_sharing_state`: opens the edit form of a default bundle, which shows All/All and 7 results. It picks Read and Unshared, checks the preview shows 3, saves, checks the bundle's bookmark list, and reopens the form to check the saved selection.

**Left out, as in the plan:** invalid values, PUT behaviour and interaction with `q`, because the ticket doesn't define what should happen. Unit tests are left to the implementer. The API sharing tests run with sharing switched off in the profile, because the contract filters on the bookmark's `shared` field alone. If the implementation also requires sharing to be enabled, those tests will fail, and by the ticket they are right to.
